newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia party says to accept election results.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia party says to accept election results.

text.p: Indonesia's Moslem-backed minority party said on Thursday it would accept the results of last month's general elections but would go ahead and file lawsuits alleging electoral fraud.
The United Development Party (PPP) has alleged widespread irregularities in the elections and protested against what it described as "terror, intimidation and vote buying".
The party won just under 23 percent of the vote in the poll, which the ruling Golkar swept with a majority of over 74 percent after the most violent campaign in three decades.
"I can confirm that most of the PPP branches will accept the results of the general elections...that they will sign the election results," PPP spokesman Usamah Hisyam told Reuters by telephone.

"But this endorsing does not necessarily mean that we consider the election as clean. We will go on with the plan to file lawsuits against electoral officials for the various election irregularities."
The PPP earlier threatened to reject the results.
The only other party permitted to contest the election, the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), won only three percent of the May 29 vote, down from 15 percent in 1992.
Both minority parties and independent observers charged there had been irregularities during the election.

The PPP has said many party witnesses at polling booths were intimidated so they could not do their job and that students were forced to vote for a "certain political party" or fail their examinations.
At least three soldiers were killed in riots which erupted during Indonesia's general election campaign last month, the Jakarta Post reported on Tuesday.
Authorities say more than 300 people died during the campaign, mostly from traffic accidents, while 124 died in a shopping centre fire during a riot in South Kalimantan province.
